title: Midday coordinator scratchpad - Nina Patel
body:
-- quick context
Today: heavy scheduling day, 8 interviews + 3 take-home reviews due. keep candidate experience tight.
Priority: confirm next-step interviews for senior infra eng (Akira), follow up offer acceptance timeline for data-science lead (Marta).

--- morning recap (what landed)
- Akira (senior infra) completed take-home at 08:10 — marked 'ok' by tech interviewer (Ethan). Need to schedule loop: 2 interviewers free windows: Thu 10-12, Fri 13-16. Candidate prefers mornings PST. ACTION: propose Thu 10am PT.
- Marta (data science lead) verbally said wants to talk to comp team before accepting. Sent comp connect intro (Priya) at 09:05 — awaiting reply.
- No-show: Hanna (frontend) scheduled 09:30 — no show, no message. Left voicemail 09:45, Slack nudged hiring manager. If no response by EOD, mark as withdrew and close loop.

--- midday to-do (ordered)
1) Send Akira slot proposal (Thu 10am PT) + calendar hold (2hrs) — include interviewer prep notes, test rubric link.
2) Chase Marta on comp call availability — offer expires 3/25 per offer doc, cc hiring manager.
3) Reschedule Hanna or mark status — check CV for rebook policy, note any pattern of no-shows.
4) Confirm onsite rooms for Fri loops (room bookings in calendar) — SRE needs 1 projector room.
5) Update candidate tracker (sheet) for all 'in-flight' roles — note sticky candidates and blockers.
6) Prep 1-pager for tomorrow's hiring sync: top 5 risks + suggested mitigations.

--- messaging snippets (quick copy/paste)
- To candidate (availability): "Hi {FirstName}, thanks again for completing the take-home. Would Thu 10:00 AM PT work for a 2-hour interview loop? We’ll be joined by two engineers and one manager. Please confirm and I’ll send calendar invites. — Nina"
- To no-show: "Hi {FirstName}, we missed you for the 9:30 interview. Are you still interested in continuing with the process? If yes, share 2 times that work in the next 3 business days and I’ll reschedule. If you’re no longer available, let me know and I’ll close the loop. — Nina"
- To hiring manager re: comp call: "Marta indicated she’d like to speak with comp before accepting. Can you share 2 windows today/tomorrow for Priya to connect? Offer deadline 3/25. — Nina"

--- scheduling quirks / notes to self
- Interviewers prefer Google Calendar invites, but some still on Outlook — always include .ics in invites for frictionless add.
- When booking multi-interviewer loops, send 2x options separated by >6 hours to avoid conflicts.
- If candidate requests timezone help, always show both PT and CET (we often forget CET for EMEA candidates).

--- blockers / escalations
- Comp team bandwidth: Priya has limited slots today (11:30-12:30). If Marta can't, escalate to Sarah (comp lead) to avoid missing offer expiry.
- Room availability flagged: facilities ticket raised (FAC-987) — if not resolved by 3pm, move onsite to hybrid and notify candidate.

--- quick metrics / daily targets
- target: 90% same-day scheduling response for incoming offers.
- today so far: 6/8 responses same-day (75%) — need to push for faster replies.

--- end-of-day handoff notes
- Leave running list in candidate tracker of everyone pending comp call + proposed times.
- Draft tomorrow morning's priority email to talent leads with # of offers pending, deadlines.

--- random brain dump (ideas)
- Consider templating 'no-show' automation: 1st no-show = automated SMS + reschedule link, 2nd no-show = manual follow-up.
- Build a 1-click calendar action for common loop templates (2-hr loop, 90-min panel, 45-min follow-up).

--- small reminders to self
- Lunch: 12:30-13:00 blocked.
- Standup notes: bring up hiring velocity drop in EMEA.
- Check PTO overlaps for next week before proposing final onsite days.

(End of scratchpad)
